searchText: Do we have plans to standardize `eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas`, it seems geth implemented it and I'd prefer to not expose custom methods if it can be avoided 🙂 That should not be standardized. In discussions, the general agreement was that clients should provide enough *data* so that external tools can build their own oracle, but clients should not be used as an oracle themselves. There is a standardized endpoint (I forget the name) that is being worked on/proposed which would make available some history statistics so a library could build an oracle. (percentiles of historic premiums accepted by block producers) feeHistory is the method you’re thinking of. I guess I’ll just not implement it 👍 https://gist.github.com/zsfelfoldi/473e29106d38525de6b4413e2ebcddf1 https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/commit/45d49bf403e0a5ec356e4940cf15800d0a59a661 By not implement I mean the Geth specific endpoint Is there a ropsten ethstats? Calaveras is down right? What happens if there is some issue with dynamics of 1559 fee mechanism that could not be seen before launching on mainnet? Sgould clients prepare a remedy release (release without 1559 changes) to be immediatelly ready if something critical happens? Just thinking out loud... It this kind of fixing a network even an option? <@!508125616940515329> sorry, I don't know the answer to either 😅 I think it really depends. I doubt the actual mechanism will have an issue given that it's been tested extensively, both on our devnets + testnets, on other blockchains, and analyzed economically. There are some known attacks (e.g. 51% of miners drive the base fee down to 0), but it is likely fine to respond to those in hours/days vs. minutes/hours. I think what is likeliest is an issue in implementations, like we saw on Ropsten, or right after Berlin. So in that case, clients will need to issue a new release ASAP. It probably makes sense for client teams to have someone available for the ~24h after the fork in case something happens. Would it make sense to have a specific temporary chat channel for client teams and node maintainers for the fork so that any issues can be reported/discussed immediately and any updates can be pushed immediately? I think most of us are going to make sure we're up for it. We can use <#745077610685661265> for that during the fork
